units.Data Storytelling y diseño de dashboards: Data Storytelling and Dashboard Design — an interactive guide | Borja Mora
units.Un dashboard no se diseña para ser visto: A dashboard isn't designed to be seen. It's designed to be understood. Ten chapters that prove it while they explain it.
units.Un manual interactivo: el mismo dashboar: An interactive guide: the same dashboard learns to tell a story as you scroll.
units.Data Storytelling<br> <em>y diseño de</e:
Data Storytelling
and the design of
dashboards
units.Lo que he aprendido sobre percepción, vi: What I've learnt about perception, visualisation, composition and narrative to design dashboards that people understand.
units.Este es un dashboard de ventas.<br>Tómat:
This is a sales dashboard.
Take a second.
What is it telling you?
units.Un dashboard puede estar lleno de datos: A dashboard can be full of data and still say nothing.
units.El problema no siempre es tener demasiad: The problem isn't always having too much data. Sometimes the problem is that everything wants attention at the same time.
units.Primero quito lo que compite con el mens: First, I remove whatever competes with the message.
units.Después decido qué merece realmente la a: Then I decide what really deserves attention.
units.Y entonces aparece algo importante: <spa: And then something important happens: I know where to look.
units.Un dashboard no está terminado cuando lo: A dashboard isn't finished when the data is in.
units.Al principio pensaba que un buen dashboa: At first, I thought a good dashboard was mostly about the visuals.
Over time, I've changed my mind.
units.Ahora, antes de abrir Power BI, intento: Now, before I open Power BI, I try to answer other questions:
units.quién va a mirar el informe,: who is going to look at the report,
units.qué quiero que vea primero,: what I want them to see first,
and what they should be able to do afterwards.
units.Este manual reúne lo que he ido aprendie: This guide brings together what I've learnt about data storytelling and how I try to put it into practice.
units.Algunas ideas vienen de la investigación: Some ideas come from research on perception and visualisation; others are rules of thumb that help me design; and others are simply part of how I work.
units.De la pregunta a la historia: From the question to the story
units.<b>Contexto</b> → percepción → limpieza: Context → perception → decluttering → attention → visual → composition → words → narrative → action
units.Por qué comunicar con datos es un proble: Why communicating with data is a problem of meaning.
How we see, group and compare.
What to take away before adding.
How to make what matters obvious.
The right chart depends on the task.
units.Títulos y anotaciones que hacen parte de: Titles and annotations that do part of the work.
From a single figure to a story.
units.Los datos pueden ser correctos y aun así: Data can be correct and still communicate nothing.
units.Los mismos 60 datos de ventas mensuales: The same 60 monthly sales figures by channel, first scattered and then arranged on a timeline where the online channel stands out.
When I explore, I'm still searching.
units.60 puntos: ventas mensuales de cinco can: 60 dots: monthly sales across five channels. Everything carries the same weight because I don't yet know what matters.
units.Pruebo variables, busco patrones, sigo p: I try variables, look for patterns, follow leads.
When I explain, the question is a different one.
units.Ahora tengo que decidir qué merece la at: Now I have to decide what deserves someone else's attention.
units.Los datos no han cambiado. <span class=\: The data hasn't changed. The intention has.
units.Explorar me ayuda a descubrir. Explicar: Exploring helps me discover. Explaining forces me to decide what deserves someone else's attention.
units.Tres capas que tienen que encajar: Three layers that have to fit together
units.No es una fórmula exacta. Es la forma en: It isn't an exact formula. It's how I review a report before I call it finished. The three layers have to work together: if one fails, the report loses its force.
units.Antes de elegir un gráfico, intento aver: Before I choose a chart, I try to work out what problem I'm solving.
units.Una petición vaga se convierte en una pr: A vague request becomes a question: audience, question, evidence and action.
units.¿En qué canal debería invertir el próxim: Which channel should we invest in next quarter?
It almost always starts the same way.
Fine. But it isn't a question yet.
units.¿Quién va a leerlo?: Who is going to read it?
units.¿Qué necesita entender o decidir?: What do they need to understand or decide?
units.¿Qué datos puedo utilizar para demostrar: What data can I use to prove it?
The real question is something else.
units.Gráfico de ventas por canal, Q4 2024 fre: Sales by channel, Q4 2024 against Q4 2025. The title changes from a description to a sentence that sums up the idea.
units.El canal online ya concentra la mayor pa: Online now accounts for most of the growth.
units.Ventas por canal, en miles de euros: Sales by channel, in thousands of euros
units.Antes de diseñar, intento encontrar una: Before I design anything, I try to find one sentence.
units.Correcto. Pero le deja todo el trabajo a: Correct. But it leaves all the work to the reader.
units.El gráfico cambia muy poco. La interpret: The chart barely changes. The interpretation changes a lot.
units.Otra prueba que me funciona: imaginar qu: Another test that works for me: imagine I have three minutes and no screen.
units.¿Qué debería hacer alguien con esa infor: What should someone do with that information?
units.Lo que sobrevive a esos tres minutos pro: Whatever survives those three minutes probably deserves a place in the story.
units.La misma pregunta no se diseña igual par: The same question isn't designed the same way for everyone.
units.Antes de diseñar un informe, necesito sa: Before I design a report, I need to know who is going to use it and what they need to understand.
units.Dirección quiere el número y la tendenci: Leadership wants the number and the trend. No filters, generous margins and a single lead visual. The detail goes below, and small.
units.El equipo comercial lo consulta cada día: The sales team checks it every day. Quick filters at the top, a full row of KPIs and comparisons you can read at a glance.
units.Quien analiza acepta densidad si a cambi: Analysts accept density if it gets them answers. Filters down the side, more visuals and more detail, but the hierarchy stays.
units.Un cliente externo, por ejemplo, no tien: An external client, for example, doesn't need to know our acronyms or our internal language. They need context, a few KPIs, a clear message and no unnecessary jargon.
units.Y hay otra pregunta que a veces se me ol: And there's another question I sometimes forget: where will they look at it?
units.No es lo mismo un comité mensual frente: A monthly committee in front of a big screen, where probably only the first KPIs get read, isn't the same as checking the report on a phone between two meetings.
units.Plano de un dashboard que cambia según l: Wireframe of a dashboard that changes with the audience: more space and one dominant visual for leadership, filters at the top for the sales team, side filters and more detail for analysts, and a single message for an external client.
units.Diccionario visual: los verbos que uso p: Visual dictionary: the verbs I use to write titles
Before the chart comes the question.
units.Primero entiendo qué quiero responder. D: First I understand what I want to answer. Then, what the reader needs to know. And only then do I decide how to show it.
units.¿Qué necesita hacer el lector?: What does the reader need to do?
units.¿Cómo lo voy a representar?: How am I going to show it?
units.La codificación visual que mejor resuelv: The visual encoding that best solves that task.
